intro: Reading closely means naming a rhetorical device in a real text and saying what it does: how an editorial, a speech or a story achieves its effect — and, when you speak in public, using those devices on purpose. This quiz gives you seventeen short quotations in the style of editorials, speeches, reviews, columns and chronicles; each cue tells you what the device does, never its name, and you type the German term. Where German has two established names both are accepted: Übertreibung / Hyperbel, Untertreibung / Litotes, Personifikation / Personifizierung, Klimax / Steigerung, Alliteration / Stabreim, Euphemismus / Beschönigung, Chiasmus / Kreuzstellung, Pars pro toto / Synekdoche, Ellipse / Auslassung; you may type the term with or without its article. The devices: imagery (Metapher, Vergleich, Personifikation), structure (Anapher, Antithese, Klimax, Alliteration, Chiasmus, Zeugma, Ellipse), attitude (Ironie, Hyperbel, Litotes, Euphemismus, Oxymoron), appeal (rhetorische Frage) and substitution (Pars pro toto).
tips[0].title: Imagery: Metapher, Vergleich, Personifikation, Pars pro toto
tips[0].text: Metapher: an image transferred without a comparison word (die Koalition ist ein Kartenhaus). Vergleich: the link is explicit with wie / als ob (zäh wie Kaugummi). Personifikation: something non-human feels or acts (die Märkte strafen ab). Pars pro toto: a part stands for the whole (zweihundert Seelen = two hundred people); the wider family is the Metonymie (das Weiße Haus schweigt).
tips[0].trap: wie decides: with a comparison word it is a Vergleich, without one a Metapher.
tips[0].check.why: The image is transferred directly, without wie or als ob, so it is a Metapher, not a Vergleich.
tips[1].title: Structure: Anapher, Antithese, Klimax, Chiasmus, Zeugma, Ellipse
tips[1].text: Anapher: the same words open successive clauses. Antithese: opposed ideas set against each other. Klimax: a series that rises in intensity. Alliteration: the same initial sound. Chiasmus: crosswise mirroring A–B / B–A. Zeugma: one verb governs two objects in different senses. Ellipse: words left out that the reader supplies.
tips[1].trap: A chiasmus often contains an antithesis, and an anaphora is often part of a parallelism. Name the feature the cue describes: crosswise order = Chiasmus; same opening words = Anapher.
tips[1].check.why: One verb, nehmen, governs two objects in different senses (take a hat, take one's leave): that is a Zeugma.
tips[2].title: Attitude: Ironie, Hyperbel, Litotes, Euphemismus, Oxymoron
tips[2].text: Ironie: the opposite of what is meant. Hyperbel / Übertreibung: inflation beyond the literal (eine halbe Ewigkeit). Litotes / Untertreibung: asserting something by negating its opposite (nicht unerheblich = erheblich; nicht ohne = beachtlich; alles andere als klug = dumm). Euphemismus: softening (negatives Wachstum, entschlafen). Oxymoron: contradictory words fused (ohrenbetäubende Stille, bittersüß).
tips[2].trap: A litotes negates the opposite; it is not necessarily a double negative. „nicht unerheblich“ has two negations, but „alles andere als überzeugend“ and „nicht gerade klein“ have only one – they are still litotes.
tips[2].check.why: This litotes negates the opposite with a single nicht; the understatement means the contribution was unhelpful.
tips[3].title: Name it, then say what it does
tips[3].text: An analysis sentence = device + verb of effect. Die Anapher verbindet und betont. Die Antithese schärft den Kontrast. Die Klimax steigert. Der Euphemismus mildert. Die Ironie entlarvt. Die rhetorische Frage bezieht den Leser ein. Die Litotes schwächt ab – und betont gerade dadurch.
tips[3].check.why: A Klimax is a rising series, so its effect verb is steigern; mildern fits a Euphemismus and verschleiern a cover-up.
tips[3].visual.rows[0].a: Metapher: Das Gesetz ist ein zahnloser Tiger.
tips[3].visual.rows[1].a: Litotes: Das war nicht ganz unproblematisch.
tips[3].visual.rows[2].a: Chiasmus: Wir leben nicht, um zu essen, wir essen, um zu leben.
tips[3].visual.rows[2].b: turns a thought round to sharpen it
remember[0]: Imagery (Metapher, Vergleich, Personifikation, Pars pro toto) · structure (Anapher, Antithese, Klimax, Chiasmus, Zeugma, Ellipse) · attitude (Ironie, Hyperbel, Litotes, Euphemismus, Oxymoron).
remember[1]: Litotes = negating the opposite (nicht unerheblich, alles andere als klug) – not necessarily a double negative.
remember[2]: Name + effect verb: die Klimax steigert, der Euphemismus mildert, die Ironie entlarvt.
mistakes[0].why: With a comparison word (wie, als ob) it is a simile.
mistakes[1].why: The defining move is negating the opposite, with one negation or two.
mistakes[2].why: Match each device to its own effect verb.
hook: Spot the metaphor, the anaphora or the litotes in a speech or editorial, and say in one German sentence what it does.
tips[2].check.q: 'Sein Beitrag war nicht gerade hilfreich.' What does the speaker mean?
